what: BioMarin develops drugs for rare genetic diseases: Voxzogo for achondroplasia, enzyme replacement therapies for metabolic disorders, and a gene therapy for haemophilia A.
customers: Specialist physicians and treatment centres, paid for by insurers and national health systems.
moat: Orphan drug approvals and manufacturing for diseases with tiny patient populations, where no competitor finds it worth building a rival product.
risks: Roctavian, the gene therapy, has sold far below expectations and has been scaled back
A small reported loss of $19M, so profitability is marginal
Each product serves a tiny patient population, so a competing launch matters disproportionately
opportunities: $558M of free cash flow and $1.6B of cash against $645M of debt
Revenue grew from $1.8B to $3.2B in four years, driven by Voxzogo
Analysts see about 47% upside, with 27 covering the stock
watch: Voxzogo revenue growth and progress on the next-generation achondroplasia candidate.
